title: Induced Representations, Frobenius Reciprocity and Applications

items.title: The induced $R$-linear $G$-module $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G W$ as $H$-covariant functions on $G$
A left transversal identifies $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G W$ with a direct sum of $[G:H]$ copies of $W$
items.strategy: Choose one representative of each left coset, evaluate an $H$-covariant function on those representatives, and reconstruct the function from those values. The inverse map packages one copy of $W$ at each chosen representative.

items.title: The dimension of an induced finite-dimensional representation is $[G:H]\dim W$
items.strategy: Apply the direct-sum description over a field and count one copy of the underlying vector space of $W$ for each left coset of $H$ in $G$.

items.title: The function model of induction agrees with the tensor-product model $k[G]\otimes_{k[H]}W$
The induced character $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\chi$ of a complex character
Frobenius' formula for the character of an induced representation
items.strategy: Use the left-transversal decomposition of the induced module. Only the summands fixed by the chosen group element contribute to the trace, and on each such summand the action is conjugate to the subgroup action on $W$.

items.title: Inducing the trivial representation gives the permutation representation on $G/H$
items.strategy: For the trivial $H$-action, an $H$-covariant function is constant on each left coset. The basis vectors supported on single cosets are therefore permuted exactly by the left action of $G$ on $G/H$.

items.title: Induction is left adjoint to restriction for finite-group modules over a commutative ring
items.strategy: Send an $RG$-map out of the induced module to its evaluation on the function supported on $H$ at the identity, and build the inverse by letting $G$ act on the value of an $RH$-map. The group-ring/module dictionary identifies these constructions with equivariant maps.

items.title: Frobenius reciprocity for complex characters
items.strategy: Translate the adjunction on intertwiner spaces into the character inner product using the published formula that the inner product equals the dimension of the intertwiner space.

items.title: Virtual characters and the character ring $R(G)$ of a finite group
Induction is transitive along subgroup chains
items.strategy: Either compare the two induced function spaces directly by composing covariance conditions, or pass to the tensor-product model and use associativity of tensor products along the subgroup inclusions.

items.title: Induction and restriction satisfy the projection formula on character rings
items.strategy: First prove the identity on honest characters using the tensor-product character formula and Frobenius reciprocity. Then extend the formula $\mathbb{Z}$-bilinearly to virtual characters.

items.title: Every irreducible complex character occurs in the induction of an irreducible constituent of its restriction
items.strategy: Restrict the irreducible representation to $H$, choose an irreducible constituent of that restriction, and apply Frobenius reciprocity to show the original character reappears in the corresponding induced character.

items.title: Double cosets $K\backslash G/H$ of two subgroups
Conjugate representations and conjugate characters on conjugate subgroups
Mackey's double-coset formula for restricting an induced character
items.strategy: Decompose the induced module into the $K$-stable pieces indexed by the $(K,H)$-double cosets. Each piece is itself an induced module from the intersection subgroup with the conjugated action.

items.title: Mackey's irreducibility criterion for finite groups
items.strategy: Compute the self-inner product of the induced character, expand the restricted induced character with Mackey's formula, and use the irreducibility test given by self-inner product one.

items.title: The central character of an irreducible complex character
Class sums act on an irreducible representation by central-character scalars
items.strategy: A class sum lies in the center of $\mathbb{C}[G]$, so Schur's lemma forces it to act by a scalar. Comparing traces with the class-sum trace computation identifies that scalar with the central-character value.

items.title: The values of a central character are algebraic integers
items.strategy: The integral class sums generate a commutative ring inside the center of the group algebra, hence act by scalars satisfying monic integral equations. The previous proposition identifies those scalars with the central-character values.

items.title: The degree of an irreducible complex character divides $|G|$
items.strategy: Rewrite $|G|/\chi(1)$ as a sum of central-character values times character values on inverse class representatives. The right side is an algebraic integer, so the rational algebraic-integer criterion forces it to be an integer.

items.title: The degree of an irreducible complex character divides $[G:Z(G)]$
items.strategy: Use the standard tensor-power argument: the center acts by scalars on every tensor power, so the tensor power factors through a quotient of $G^n$ by a central subgroup. Applying the degree-divides-order theorem to each tensor power forces the original degree to divide $[G:Z(G)]$.

items.title: A finite group with an irreducible complex character of degree greater than $1$ is nonabelian
items.strategy: If the group were abelian, the published abelian criterion would force every irreducible complex character to have degree one.

items.title: An algebraic-integer average of roots of unity is either $0$ or a common root of unity
items.strategy: Average the roots of unity and take the product of all algebraic conjugates. If the average is nonzero and not constant, its norm has absolute value strictly between $0$ and $1$, impossible for a nonzero integer.

items.title: A conjugacy class of size coprime to $\chi(1)$ forces either $\chi(g)=0$ or scalar action
items.strategy: The central-character value $|C|\chi(g)/\chi(1)$ is an algebraic integer. A Bezout combination with $|C|$ and $\chi(1)$ then makes $\chi(g)/\chi(1)$ an algebraic integer, so the roots-of-unity average lemma applied to the eigenvalues of $g$ yields the dichotomy.

items.title: A conjugacy class of prime-power size forces a proper nontrivial normal subgroup
items.strategy: Apply column orthogonality to a noncentral class element to find a nontrivial irreducible character with nonzero value and degree coprime to the class size. The previous theorem then forces scalar action, and the subgroup generated by differences of class elements is a proper nontrivial normal subgroup.

items.title: Burnside's $p^aq^b$ theorem
items.strategy: Assume a minimal nonsolvable group of order $p^aq^b$. Sylow theory supplies a nonidentity central element in a Sylow subgroup, whose conjugacy class has prime-power size; the prime-power class theorem then contradicts simplicity of the minimal counterexample.

title: Induced Representations, Frobenius Reciprocity and Applications — Examples

items.title: Inducing a nontrivial character of a three-cycle subgroup of $S_3$ gives an irreducible degree-two character
items.strategy: Use Frobenius' character formula on the subgroup $A_3 \le S_3$ and compute the values on the three conjugacy-class types of $S_3$. The resulting character has degree $2$ and self-inner-product $1$.

items.title: Restricting that degree-two $S_3$ character to the three-cycle subgroup gives the two nontrivial linear characters
items.strategy: Restrict the irreducible degree-two character from the previous example to $A_3$ and use Frobenius reciprocity to compute its multiplicities against the two nontrivial linear characters of $A_3$.

items.title: Inducing the trivial character of a subgroup of order two in $S_3$ gives $1$ plus an irreducible degree-two character
items.strategy: Identify the induced representation with the permutation representation on the three left cosets. Its character counts fixed cosets, so subtracting the trivial character leaves a degree-two character with self-inner-product $1$.

items.title: Frobenius reciprocity matches multiplicities in the two preceding $S_3$ inductions
items.strategy: Compute the relevant inner products on both sides of Frobenius reciprocity using the two preceding $S_3$ decompositions and compare the multiplicities explicitly.

items.title: $C_4$ shows that divisibility of irreducible degrees by $|G|$ is not an equivalence
items.strategy: Since $C_4$ is finite abelian, every irreducible complex representation has degree $1$. The divisor $2$ of $|C_4|=4$ is therefore not an irreducible degree.

items.title: An induced irreducible complex character is always irreducible
items.strategy: Use the subgroup of order two in $S_3$: the trivial character of that subgroup is irreducible, but its induction is the reducible character $1$ plus an irreducible degree-two character.

items.title: Induction followed by restriction is the identity on complex representations
items.strategy: Start with a nontrivial linear character of the three-cycle subgroup of $S_3$. Its induction is an irreducible degree-two character, and restricting that induced character back to the subgroup gives the sum of the two nontrivial linear characters, not the original one.

items.title: Restriction of an irreducible complex representation is always irreducible
items.strategy: Use the same irreducible degree-two character of $S_3$: its restriction to the three-cycle subgroup splits as the sum of two nontrivial linear characters.

items.title: Every divisor of $|G|$ is an irreducible character degree
items.strategy: Take $G=C_4$. The divisor $2$ of $|G|=4$ is not an irreducible degree because every irreducible complex representation of a finite abelian group has degree $1$.
